entities.summary: Khalid ibn Yazid, c. 668–704 or 709, was a Umayyad prince and purported alchemist who played a pivotal role in shaping the Islamic Golden Age. He was the son of Yazid I, the caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate, and was known for his alleged expertise in alchemy and his involvement in the early Islamic art of medicine. Khalid ibn Yazid's significance extends to the realm of cultural exchange, as he facilitated the transmission of Greek and Persian knowledge to the Islamic world. He was also a patron of scholars and artists, and his court attracted prominent figures such as the poet Al-Mutanabbi. Through his relationships with other prominent figures, including the caliph Al-Mansur, Khalid ibn Yazid exerted significant influence on the political and cultural landscape of the Umayyad Caliphate. His legacy can be seen in the works of later Islamic scholars, who built upon the foundations laid by Khalid ibn Yazid and his contemporaries. As a symbol of the Umayyad Caliphate's cultural and scientific achievements, Khalid ibn Yazid remains an important figure in the annals of Islamic history.
